contexts.text: It is predicated of the onagers that they sup the wind, when vain and empty things are taken in the place of real ones, which are truths.
Give me to sup, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher () = whether anything of truth could be conjoined thence. To sup has a similar signification as to drink, but in a less degree.

Give me to sup, I pray thee, from the red () = the desire for doctrinal things. To sup = to be communicated and conjoined; hence Give me to sup, I pray thee = to desire the conjunction of truth, or of doctrinal things, with himself. AC 3316:2.
